newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - July 4.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - July 4.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and People News.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
PARIS - Avenir France, the French large-format bill board advertising unit of France's Havas, says its recently-created Internet site is now showing tariffs for the second half of this year.(Reuter)

PARIS - Private French TV channel TF1 increases advertising receipts by 104 million francs since the beginning of this year following a decision by broadcasting authority CSA to allow average advertising breaks of six minutes -- up from four minutes previously. (Le Figaro)

PARIS - An increasing number of advertisers want to use the Internet as a means of getting their message across, even in Net-backward France. The French market should grow from 4.5 million francs in 1996 to over 20 million in 1997, according to media specialist Carat.
(Les Echos)

PARIS - Advertising campaigns evoking the joys of summer are being drowned out by weeks of rain, and are hard to pull at the last minute when the weather does not match the message. Worst hit are drink brands showing their products as quenching heat-induced thirst. (Le Parisien)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
PARIS - French pay television group Canal Plus says it expects to make a profit of some three billion francs on two transactions with the Kirch Group.(Reuter)

********* PARIS - TV station M6, which used to describe itself as the little station, is no longer an adjunct to the giants of French television. In the eighth BVA/Strategies barometer of opinion it comes out as France's favourite general station. M6 says it has signed an accord which promises that at least 85 percent of its film spending would go to independent producers. (Strategies)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - Children start to recognise brands as young as age two, and according to the Kid Generation survey by the Institut de l'Enfant. Their 10 favourite brands are: Kinder (chocolate eggs), Coca-Cola, Adidas, Nike, Barbie, Reebok, Malabar (chewing gum), Danone, Lego and Haribo (sweets). (Strategies)

PARIS - Shares in LVMH rally to an all time high after British groups Guinness and Grand Metropolitan agree to consider LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault's alternative proposal to their planned merger.(Reuter)
PARIS - Prime Minister Lionel Jospin says he does not believe that reviving car-buying incentives in France is justified.(Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS

PARIS - Eric Delannoy, formerly managing director at Bordelais Lemeunier/Leo Burnett Paris, has been appointed deputy managing director at BDDP, replacing Nathalie Rastoin who has joined Ogilvy & Mather. (Le Figaro)
PARIS - Marianne van Leeuwen, has been appointed as managing director of advertising industry weekly magazine Strategies from July 1, succeeding Alain Maury. (Strategies)
